claims.text: HIP at 1230 °C will produce a BCC matrix with L21 precipitates and thereby provide high density and hardness.
HIP at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for 4 hours increases the hardness of suction-cast TaNbHfZrTi.
Rapid quenching after HIP retains the proposed precipitate structure.
Candidate as-cast AlCoCrFeNi or TaNbHfZrTi alloys can initially have BCC-based or BCC+HCP microstructures.
The initial cast material contains porosity and coarse grain boundaries.
At 1200 K, simulated FeNiCrCoCu coatings undergo rapid lattice disordering, incipient melting, and reduced hardness and elastic modulus.
AlCoCrFeNi-based material can retain a duplex microstructure and substantial mechanical strength after aging at 1200 °C.
A processing window from 1200 K to 1230 °C both avoids disordering and provides sufficient diffusion for densification and precipitation.
An inert or vacuum-sealed HIP environment prevents premature oxidation.
Processing forms a stable duplex BCC+L21 or BCC+HCP microstructure.
HIP eliminates porosity and grain-boundary segregation of deleterious ZrHf-rich phases.
HIP increases bulk density by eliminating porosity.
HIP-driven diffusion precipitates hard L21 phases that increase hardness.
Rapid lattice disordering and incipient melting cause hardness loss in FeNiCrCoCu at 1200 K.
A high grain-boundary density facilitates protective chromia formation and reduces high-temperature oxidation.
HIP refines the initial cast grain structure and creates the grain-boundary density needed for protective chromia formation.
The final material will reach a relative density greater than 96%.
The hardness will increase by more than 50%, exemplified by an increase from about 330 HV to above 500 HV.
The HIP-treated material will have oxidation and aqueous-corrosion rates comparable to or lower than those of the as-cast material.
The processed material will retain structural integrity without catastrophic failure or melting.

contradictions.description: The proposed HIP temperature is 1230 °C, approximately 1503 K, but the hypothesis also requires processing below a disordering threshold of 1200 K and says the hypothesis fails when that threshold is exceeded.
The stated window begins at 1200 K while simultaneously claiming that it avoids disordering observed at 1200 K.
The expression '1200 K (1473 K)' equates two different temperatures; 1473 K corresponds to approximately 1200 °C, not 1200 K.

The primary hypothesis requires L21 precipitates, whereas the directly evidenced HIP treatment produces BCC+HCP phases; the mediator treats L21 and HCP as alternatives, but the hardness mechanism is specified only for L21.
